newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE CANOLA, GRAIN END UP ON EXPORTER, LOCAL DEMAND.
newsitem.headline: WCE CANOLA, GRAIN END UP ON EXPORTER, LOCAL DEMAND.

text.p: Winnipeg Commodity Exchange canola and feed grain futures closed higher on exporter and local demand linked to drought concerns, traders said.

"Locals covered shorts at the close. Exporters bought and elevator companies had some hedges," a trader said. "We're in the critical podding stage for canola and it's hot with not enough rain," he said.
November WCE canola crush profit margin fell to -14.47 Friday from -14.33 Thursday. Sep-Nov spread at $2, Nov-Jan $4.30, Jan-Mar $1.20.
August canola rose $2.20 to $357.20 and November finished $2.20 higher at $360.10.
November flax rose $5 to $295 on RBC-DS.

October western barley closed $0.70 higher at $130.50 as commercials bought. Gains were partly linked to a rise in CBOT corn futures and persistent dry weather. December barley ended up $1.30 at $132.40 as commission houses sold. Volume was 400.
October feed wheat rose $0.90 to $154.80, December up $1 to $154.80 on commission buying met by hedges and commercial selling. Volume was 725 lots.
RBC-DS bought 30 October feed peas down US$1.50 at US$170, traders said.
PCTS sold 10 December oats up US$0.50 to US$118.50, floor sources said.
(All values in Canadian dollars except oats, feed peas.)
